subject.title: feat: heading-aware chunking + entity extraction for memory search

question: Should OpenClaw make Markdown heading-aware memory chunking the default, expose it as an explicit opt-in strategy/config, or defer it until the broader Memory MVP/entity design is settled?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the fix changes persisted indexing and retrieval behavior and the issue also bundles broader entity/graph-memory product scope.

options.title: Approve Narrow Chunking Design
options.body: Keep this issue canonical, implement heading-aware chunking as a focused memory-core change with explicit reindex semantics, and track entity extraction separately.

options.title: Make Heading-Aware Default
options.body: Adopt heading boundaries as canonical for Markdown memory files, accepting that existing headed files will reindex and retrieve differently after upgrade.

options.title: Defer To Memory MVP
options.body: Wait for the memory write/entity pipeline decisions so chunking, extraction, and wiki synthesis land as one coordinated design.

recommendation.title: Approve Narrow Chunking Design
recommendation.body: Keep this issue canonical, implement heading-aware chunking as a focused memory-core change with explicit reindex semantics, and track entity extraction separately.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision touches memory-core chunking, config/default policy, and index identity boundaries where this history signal is strongest.
